title: Fieldnotes Field protocol v1 shared definitions
description: Shared transport-level definitions for Field protocol v1. Grammars here are well-formedness guards for an untrusted child process, not a redefinition of the A1 notebook contract. Where a value also appears in a notebook record, A1 remains authoritative and Fieldnotes core performs the full A1 validation after these guards pass.

protocolVersion.description: Major protocol version. v1 is the version frozen at A2.

protocolRevision.description: Additive-only revision within a major version. Both peers emit only members introduced at or below the negotiated revision, which is the minimum of the two declared revisions.

runId.description: Core-generated identifier for one bounded Field process run. Opaque to the Field. Not a notebook record ID.

seq.description: Per-run monotonic sequence number shared by every Field-to-core event. Starts at 1 and increases by exactly 1 with no gaps.

offsetDatetime.description: RFC 3339 datetime with an explicit numeric offset. '-00:00' is rejected. Transport guard only; the A1 datetime contract is authoritative.

dateOnly.description: A1 date-only grammar (YYYY-MM-DD), for reference only: it is not $ref'd from record-event.schema.json's generic 'properties' map, and deliberately so. A property's scalar type -- text, date, or datetime -- comes from the declaring manifest or the A1 shared registry, never from a single frame in isolation, so no wire schema can single out 'this string must be a date' the way it singles out 'occurred_at must be an offset datetime'. Core enforces this grammar at the point where it does know the declared or registered type, rejecting a malformed value with 'record.invalid_date', distinct from 'record.invalid_datetime'.

fieldId.description: Configured Field ID. 'self' does not use this protocol. Transport guard for the A1 Field-ID grammar.

fieldStem.description: Registered Field stem from the A1 registry. The protocol does not enumerate the registered stems; core validates the value against the A1 registry.

propertyPrefix.description: Registered connector property prefix, including its trailing underscore. Null means the Field contributes no prefix.

propertyName.description: A1 property-name grammar as a transport guard.

noteType.description: Primary Note type candidate. The closed eleven-value vocabulary is frozen by A1 and is deliberately not enumerated here; core rejects any value the A1 registry does not contain.

scalarType.description: A1 scalar type names, used by a manifest to declare a prefixed property's type.

scalarValue.description: One A1-compatible scalar. JSON string carries text, date, and datetime values; the declaring manifest entry or the A1 shared registry supplies the type.

scalarList.description: Homogeneous one-dimensional list of scalars, matching A1's flat list rule. An empty list is never emitted; core omits absent values.

sourceScope.description: Connector-namespaced, non-secret, cross-instance-stable upstream authority or account scope. Half of the portable exact-source key.

sourceIdentity.description: Object identity stable within its source scope, including an object-kind namespace where upstream IDs are not unique across kinds. Half of the portable exact-source key.

sourceVersion.description: Opaque source-supplied version token. Comparable only through the ordering rule the manifest declares.

sourceVersionOrdering.description: How core may compare two source_version values for this Field. 'unsupported' means divergent content with no other ordering evidence is a conflict.

sourceRef.description: Portable exact-source key plus optional non-identity source metadata.

artifactHandle.description: Single-segment staging name chosen by the Field from a closed character set. It is never a path: it contains no separator, no dot, no traversal sequence, and no reserved Windows device name -- including 'com0' and 'lpt0', reserved alongside 'com1'-'com9' and 'lpt1'-'lpt9' even though the numbered range conventionally starts at 1 -- and core resolves it only inside the run's staging directory.

mediaType.description: Declared media type. Core maps it through the A1 canonical-extension registry; an unknown or conflicting type falls back to '.bin'. The media type is never artifact identity.

mediaTypeMatcher.description: One entry of a media-type retention include set (ADR 0007): an exact 'type/subtype' media type, or a subtype wildcard such as 'image/*'. Never an extension and never derived from a source filename. Orthogonal to A1's frozen media-type-to-extension registry, which governs naming a retained original rather than whether one is retained at all.

attachmentRef.description: A stable connector-namespaced upstream attachment reference, following the same object-kind-namespace convention sourceIdentity uses. Carried only on a not_retained artifact reference, and projected by core onto the shared skipped_attachments Note property.

recollectTarget.description: One previously-collected source object, named by its portable exact-source key alone, that core asks a Field to explicitly recollect (ADR 0007).

cursor.description: Opaque, non-secret, bounded Field-owned resume token. Core never parses, orders, or interprets it. Excludes every C0 control character and DEL, matching the treatment sourceScope already gets, not only NUL: a cursor containing an unescaped LF is exactly the value that corrupts an NDJSON-shaped state file or a log line, since a cursor is stored and logged, not merely compared.

cursorFormatVersion.description: Field-declared cursor encoding version. A stored cursor whose version differs from the manifest's is not replayed; core starts unbounded and reports a recovery gap.

identityScopeClass.description: Matching scope class for an identity anchor, from the identity and graph contract.

identityAnchor.description: A source-declared person, account, organization, or artifact anchor. An anchor may relate graph entities. It is never part of the portable exact-source key and core never reconciles Notes by it.

allOf.description: An authority- or namespace-scoped anchor must name the scope it is exact within.
A normalized channel identity must name its normalization rule and version.

redactionMarker.description: The only permitted replacement text for material a Field removed before emission.

diagnosticCode.description: Closed v1 diagnostic vocabulary. Codes prefixed 'protocol.' are emitted by core about a Field, never by a Field. Adding a code is an additive protocol revision.

diagnosticDetail.description: Bounded, already-redacted structured detail. Never a source payload, HTTP trace, credential, or protected-channel value.

limits.description: Effective bounds for this run so the Field can self-police. Core enforces them regardless of what the Field does. A ceiling is an absolute technical bound protecting core against a hostile or buggy child: no configuration may exceed it, and only a protocol revision can raise it. For most members the ceiling is also the sensible default. Two members instead have a configurable default distinct from their ceiling -- max_artifact_bytes (default 26214400 bytes / 25 MiB, ceiling 536870912 bytes / 512 MiB) and the run wall clock, expressed only as the absolute collect_request/describe_request 'deadline.not_after' rather than as a duration field here (default 600 seconds / 10 minutes, ceiling 3600 seconds / 1 hour) -- and a notebook may configure either anywhere between the product's own minimum and that ceiling, in either direction from the default.

max_artifact_bytes.description: The single-artifact ceiling, and also the retention threshold a Field compares a known artifact's size against before staging it: over this number, the Field is expected to emit a 'not_retained' reference instead of staging bytes core would then have to reject as oversized. One number serves both purposes so a Field that stages something larger really is violating a limit it was told, rather than juggling a transfer ceiling and a separate retention policy. Default 26214400 (25 MiB): a notebook is disposable working material, not a system of record, so the default keeps what is useful for work and context and larger original material stays at its source. Ceiling 536870912 (512 MiB): the absolute technical bound: a notebook may configure the default up to this ceiling, never past it.

not_after.description: The absolute instant after which the run has exceeded its wall clock. Core computes this from a configurable run-length setting: default 600 seconds (10 minutes), which a notebook may lengthen up to the absolute 3600-second (1-hour) ceiling that protects core against a hostile or buggy child that never stops. A first full sync expected to run longer than the configured length is handled by windowed, resumable runs -- the cursor and checkpoint machinery already exists for exactly that -- rather than by one long-running process, because a crash late in a long run discards far more durable-but-uncommitted work than a crash late in a short one.
